newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistan unveils new oil and gas policy.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan unveils new oil and gas policy.

text.p: Pakistan announced oil and gas sector reforms on Thursday that it said would attract foreign private investment, create infrastructure, improve management and establish a transparent system of open auction and tenders.

Caretaker Minister for Petroleum and Natural Resources Javed Jabbar told a news conference the reforms, approved by the cabinet earlier this week, included re-structuring of the state-own Oil and Gas Development Corporation (OGDC).

"Steps have been taken to create an environment in which efficient management can do its work without interference...this will result in increased production and distribution of oil and gas resources," Jabbar said.
The OGDC will get more autonomy to enable it to operate like a modern oil company and improve exploration results, he said.

He said the two state-owned gas companies, Sui Northern Gas Pipelines Ltd and Sui Southern Gas Company Ltd, had been told to reduce their transmission losses to five percent from the present level of 10 percent.
"Both companies are undertaking efforts on a war footing to achieve this very challenging target and reduce the gas losses which are, in effect, being paid for by the consumers of gas."
